headline: From Jail Cell to Lifesaver: How One Woman Broke the Cycle
meta_description: After 20 years cycling through incarceration, Jodi Whitt now runs a program that has helped over 1,000 women escape jail and human trafficking in Kansas.
summary_short: A woman who spent two decades moving in and out of Shawnee County jail now helps others escape that same cycle—and intercepts traffickers waiting in parking lots.
body:
After spending over 20 years cycling through the Shawnee County jail in Topeka, Kansas—arrested, held for up to 72 hours, released with nothing but the clothes on her back, then returning to addiction and re-incarceration—Jodi Whitt decided to use her hard-won freedom to help others trapped in that same loop. In 2019, she got sober and committed to treatment. By 2021, she had joined a local Rotary club's mentorship program for women transitioning out of jail. Today, Whitt works from a small office decorated with affirmational quotes and a ceramic white unicorn, coordinating support for newly released women. "Sometimes I can't believe this is my life now," she says. Her transformation mirrors a larger shift in Topeka: the Rotary Club of Community Action Against Human Trafficking has launched Intersection to Care, a reentry initiative that has assisted more than 1,000 women since 2022.

The program emerged from a grim reality. Members discovered that traffickers were waiting in jail parking lots for vulnerable women to be released, sometimes even posting bail as leverage. Whitt and other volunteers now meet women the moment they leave the gate, providing safe transportation, housing, and wraparound support including technology classes, art therapy, meditation, and doula services. In one memorable encounter, Whitt stood in the parking lot while a trafficker waited beside her for his target. When the woman was released, Whitt calmly drove her to safety.

This work matters urgently. Between 1980 and 2023, the number of incarcerated women in the United States grew by over 600 percent, yet jails historically lacked gender-responsive care or meaningful reentry services. In Topeka, where the female jail population has grown from six women to more than 100, Whitt's presence—and her willingness to meet women exactly where she once stood—offers something more valuable than any handbook: proof that people can truly change.

Intersection to Care has assisted 1,000+ women since launching in 2022
